headline: Policy on e-bikes and micro-mobility devices tabled 7-0 after residents asked for more time
summary: The policy covers all e-bikes and other powered devices, with no separate rules by bike type. Members said three drafts exist and must be combined before the policy returns. A public speaker asked that it be tabled until the state's Ride Safe Act moves and the city's bike and pedestrian advisory committee reviews it. Also approved: an additional art club stipend at Beverly Middle School for the 2026-2027 school year, at $1,431, and a travel policy requiring passports valid six months past the return date.
decisions: Approved an additional art club stipend for the 2026-2027 school year, five in favor.
Approved a budget transfer into a grade four teacher salary line at North Beverly, unanimously.
Approved a second art club stipend at Beverly Middle School, 7-0.
Approved the school-sanctioned international travel policy as presented, 7-0.
Tabled the powered micro mobility device policy, 7-0.
discussion: E-bike policy: Public speakers asked the committee to table the policy and focus on safety education, saying licensed teens and adults should be allowed to ride e-bikes on school property.
E-bike policy scope: Members said the draft does not separate bike types and asked for expert input before it returns.
Strategic plan draft: The superintendent presented a draft five-year plan with four priorities, running from 2027 to 2031, and asked members to mark it up before budget talks.
High school electricity costs: The business manager said a solar payout of $700,000 or $750,000 went to a city DPW account, and the high school electricity line is in the negative.
Late bus arrivals: A public speaker, a middle school teacher, said buses have arrived late for more than a year and asked for a clear plan and measurable improvement.
